officialTitle: Sacituzumab Govitecan in Metastatic Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
setting: Relapsed or refractory metastatic, previously treated

design.blinding: PFS by blinded independent central review
design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: A total of 468 patients without brain metastases were randomly assigned to receive sacituzumab govitecan (235 patients) or chemotherapy (233 patients).
primaryEndpoints: PFS (BICR) in patients without brain metastases
design.notes: Comparator: single-agent chemotherapy of physician's choice (eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine, or gemcitabine). All patients had previous taxane exposure.

clinicalQuestion: Is the Trop-2-directed ADC sacituzumab govitecan superior to single-agent chemotherapy of physician's choice in relapsed or refractory metastatic triple-negative breast cancer?

pico.population: Relapsed or refractory metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (primary analysis population without brain metastases)
pico.comparator: Single-agent chemotherapy of physician's choice (eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine, or gemcitabine)
pico.outcomes: Primary: PFS by BICR in patients without brain metastases. Secondary: OS, ORR, safety

arms.label: Physician's choice chemotherapy
arms.regimen: Eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine, or gemcitabine (physician's choice)

publications.title: Sacituzumab Govitecan in Metastatic Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: The median progression-free survival was 5.6 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 4.3 to 6.3; 166 events) with sacituzumab govitecan and 1.7 months (95% CI, 1.5 to 2.6; 150 events) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.41; 95% CI, 0.32 to 0.52; P<0.001).

The median overall survival was 12.1 months (95% CI, 10.7 to 14.0) with sacituzumab govitecan and 6.7 months (95% CI, 5.8 to 7.7) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio for death, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.38 to 0.59; P<0.001).
The percentage of patients with an objective response was 35% with sacituzumab govitecan and 5% with chemotherapy.

safety.sourceQuote: The incidences of key treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or higher were neutropenia (51% with sacituzumab govitecan and 33% with chemotherapy)
leukopenia (10% and 5%), diarrhea (10% and <1%), anemia (8% and 5%), and febrile neutropenia (6% and 2%)

safety.description: Grade 3 or higher treatment-related febrile neutropenia
Deaths owing to adverse events: three in each group; none considered related to sacituzumab govitecan
safety.sourceQuote: There were three deaths owing to adverse events in each group; no deaths were considered to be related to sacituzumab govitecan treatment.

strengths: Randomised phase III trial with PFS by blinded independent central review
Both PFS and OS significantly improved
limitations: Primary analysis restricted to patients without brain metastases
Comparator response rate was low, reflecting a heavily pretreated population

clinicalImplications.text: Established sacituzumab govitecan as a standard option for previously treated metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, with survival benefit over single-agent chemotherapy.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Anticipate myelosuppression and diarrhoea with sacituzumab govitecan — proactive neutropenia and diarrhoea management keeps patients on therapy.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 33882206.
